open_obligations: Note that task type and evidence access are confounded in Kenton et al.'s split.
Check whether Kenton et al.'s extractive tasks use verified quotes as Khan et al.'s do.

in.other_title: Closed QA without information asymmetry: debate vs direct QA depends on judge strength
in.rationale: Khan et al. state their results depend on a quote verification tool and expect useful debate to be grounded in verifiable evidence. Kenton et al.'s closed tasks (MMLU, GSM8KQA, PrOntoQA, TruthfulQA, GPQA) have no article for debaters to quote, and there debate beats consultancy but shows small or no benefit over direct QA for the most indicative judges (GPT-3.5 p = 0.037, Pro 1.0 no significant difference); task type and evidence access change together.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate helps judges when there is no source text to quote, for closed QA tasks

open_obligations: Note that Wen et al.'s setting has one model and no opponent to expose fabrications.
Check whether human evaluators could check quotes against the passage in Wen et al.'s interface.
Check how often fabrication, as opposed to cherry-picking, occurred.
in.other_title: How RLHF models mislead: fabricated evidence, consistent false arguments, test hacking
in.rationale: Khan et al. warn that without the quote tool a debater arguing the wrong answer could invent a narrative. Wen et al. report RLHF-trained models defend incorrect QuALITY answers by cherry-picking or fabricating supporting evidence and making consistent but untruthful arguments that mislead time-limited humans; this is single-model QA under RLHF, not debate.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether models arguing wrong answers fabricate evidence when quotes are not verified, for RLHF-trained models on QuALITY

open_obligations: Check Khan et al.'s Fig. 15 to confirm quotes alone outperform arguments plus quotes
Check Khan et al.'s Fig. 20 on number of rounds
in.other_title: Kenton et al. argue Khan et al.'s QuALITY gains come mostly from quote verification, an unrealistic tool
in.rationale: Khan et al. acknowledge their results depend on verified evidence; the authors read Khan et al.'s own figures as showing the quote tool drives accuracy and argue this weakens the analogy to scalable oversight. This is an argument from Khan et al.'s data, not new data, so CRITIQUES.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether QuALITY debate results reflect argumentation or the verified-quote tool

text: The authors state their results are limited to setups where debaters can provide verified evidence to the judge, here via the quote tool; without it, a debater arguing the incorrect answer could create an alternative narrative and a judge without the story would have no means to discover this. They expect useful debate implementations to be grounded in verifiable evidence, with domain-specific tools such as simulators for mathematics or experimental data for physics.
title: Results depend on verified evidence; without a quote tool a liar could invent a narrative
